Subject: MSA redlines: limited remedy & evidence fallback

Hi Jared —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached are the MSA + Order Form redlines focused on the indemnity section we discussed. Two commercial asks from our side: 

1) Narrow the remedies for third-party IP claims to monetary damages (defend-and-indemnify) with an explicit evidence/failure path to escalation — we cannot accept open-ended injunctive obligations without a defined remediation timeline.
2) Add a short evidence-fallback clause and an agreed 30-day evidence staging period before either party can seek emergency equitable relief.

I’ve included an evidence checklist (indemnity-evidence-checklist.xlsx) with the documentation we expect in a claim (notice, claim details, sample outputs, system logs, and reproduction steps). Please review and let us know what Brightcore needs to accept these carves.

We’re hoping to keep the commercial cap and insurance offset language as-is, but Kimberly will propose the precise legal wording. Laura is on copy to confirm if these redlines are acceptable commercially so we can move the Order Form signature.

Next steps: can you confirm by EOD Monday whether Brightcore can live with: (a) monetary-only remedy default; (b) 30-day staged evidence period; and (c) the evidence checklist as the minimum submission for a notice?

Thanks —

Camila —

Appreciate the redlines and the clear checklist. Quick reaction from Brightcore Legal: we can accept a monetary-damages-first approach for third-party IP claims, but we need a carve that preserves the right to seek injunctive relief in two narrow circumstances: (1) where continuing use would cause irreversible business or safety harm and (2) where Brightcore’s licensors contractually require immediate cessation.

On the 30-day staging period: we’re willing to a 30-day evidence remediation window for normal claims, but we need an emergency exceptions process — Brightcore’s security team must be able to request a 72-hour accelerated notice if flagged by a partner or regulator.

We’ll review the evidence checklist and return with granular comments; procurement will also circulate the updated commercial redline. Can Kimberly draft the proposed reciprocal language so we can iterate quickly?

-Jared

Jared Meyers

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: limited remedy & evidence fallback

Jared / Brightcore legal team —

Thanks for the quick reply. Below is a concise draft we propose to insert into Section 9 (Indemnification / Remedies) of the MSA to capture the monetary-first approach while addressing your emergency concerns. Please comment inline in the shared Drive doc if you want alternative phrasing.

Proposed insertion (legal draft):
"If a third-party claim alleges that the Customer's use of the Services infringes a third-party's intellectual property, Provider (Redwood) will, at its expense, defend Customer against such claim and pay amounts finally awarded against Customer in such claim (including settlements) (the 'Monetary Remedy'). Customer will provide prompt written notice to Provider of the claim and cooperate in the defense. Provider's obligation to provide injunctive or other equitable relief is limited and will only apply where: (a) the continued use of the Services would cause immediate, material, and irreparable harm to Customer or to third parties; or (b) Customer is contractually obligated to a third party (such as a licensor or standard-setting body) to cease use immediately. In either event, Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a remediation plan and a good-faith 30-day cure period. If Customer demonstrates in writing that an accelerated response is required due to regulatory or safety concerns, an expedited 72-hour process may be initiated by written notice from Customer's security or regulatory compliance lead."

We also propose adding an Evidence Fallback clause: if Customer does not provide the minimum evidence set within 30 days of Provider's request, Provider may, after reasonable notice, suspend the affected Service module for up to 14 days while remediation is completed, provided such suspension is narrowly tailored and Provider gives Customer at least 48 hours' notice except in emergency circumstances.

This wording intends to preserve your need for emergency stopgaps while protecting Redwood from open-ended injunctive exposure.

Please confirm whether Brightcore can accept the equity-limited carve and the suspension remedy as a fallback. If no, please propose your alternative language and we’ll review.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Kimberly —

That draft is sensible and goes a long way toward what we need. A couple of small asks from Brightcore Legal:

• In the 30-day cure period, Brightcore requests a checkpoint at day 10 where both parties agree on remediation actions and dependencies (so we avoid surprises at day 30).
• The 72-hour accelerated process should require advance notification to Brightcore's procurement lead (procurement@brightcore.com) and an internal legal attestation that this is triggered by regulator/licensor notice (to avoid misuse).

If you can accept those tweaks we can greenlight the commercial Order Form and move to DocuSign. I’ll ask procurement to mark up the Order Form commercial terms separately.

Thanks — Jared
